messages:
olivia_sales: Quick sync 10: AtlasCare wants a 4-week POC on Private with med-qa-7b-v2. Requirements: SentencePiece 32k tokenizer, CMEK HSM-backed keys, int4 quant, p50 <150ms for single-user UI. Any red flags?
tomer_se: Tokenizer parity is first-class risk. If they can share the SentencePiece files we can validate byte-level mapping. Also need to confirm generation sampling params used in training.
lee_infra: Hardware note: int4 on our Blackwell fleet looks good but KV-cache attention may trigger fp16 rumshots for some layers. I'll run a short compatibility sweep (int4 vs fp16 canary) and perf harness for seq=128,512 at conc=1.
olivia_sales: Pricing: they asked for an all-in POC quote (infra + support hours). Can you ballpark delta between int4 and fp16 Dedicated pricing?
lee_infra: Ballpark: int4 reduces GPU memory and increases throughput ~1.6-2x depending on kernel maturity. For Dedicated POC we recommend quoting the quantized tier with a 15-25% discount for trial volume; I'll return concrete numbers after validation.
maria_sec: Security answers for SOC/KMS: "Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (CMEK) integrated with major KMS providers. HSM-backed key stores are supported via customer KMS. Keys are customer-controlled and can be rotated on their schedule; Redwood does not persist plaintext keys. Audit logs for inference and admin actions can be exported and retention configured." We can provide SOC2 summary under NDA.
olivia_sales: Perfect. Please drop that text in the questionnaire. Also need confirmation of key rotation frequency support (we support any schedule, but note rotation may require briefly reloading endpoints).
maria_sec: Confirmed: rotation supported; plan for short reload windows (<30s) if customers rotate keys without rolling. We'll provide runbook.
ticket_bot: Created ticket: RINF-9024  "AtlasCare med-qa-7b-v2 POC: tokenizer + quant + KMS validation". Assignee: lee_infra. ETA: 72h.
lee_infra: Starting sweep now. Test config: ```model: med-qa-7b-v2
variants: [int4,fp16_canary]
seqs: [128,512]
concurrency: [1]
tokenizer: sentencepiece-32k
metrics: [p50,p95,perplexity-delta]``` Will post results here.
tomer_se: If tokenizer mismatch shows up, we can propose canonical tokenizer export or small embedding remap. Also plan to run a short eval set focused on clinical abbreviations.
olivia_sales: Thanks all. I'll draft the POC quote including the SOC blurb and ping legal for NDA. Will update the customer after your sweep results. :thumbsup:
